perspective:
**Sara Manuelito’s available information:**

- Sara knows she is a Speech-Language Pathologist and an American Indian woman. She works at a community health center.
- She knows Shirley Whiteplume as a nurse, long-time colleague, and close friend. They have worked together for several years and share mutual respect.
- Sara attended the funeral of a mutual patient. She observed Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it must be hard and that she saw how much Shirley cared. Shirley replied it had been tough and that she kept thinking whether more could have been done. Sara told her they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought. Shirley said Sara was right but that it was hard to let go.
- During a work coffee break, Sara raised the topic of the patient’s treatment decisions and said she sensed Shirley felt burdened by the outcome. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciated it but said it was hard to accept.
- Later, Sara observed Shirley continuing to be reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet office moment, Sara confronted her, saying she had noticed Shirley holding back feelings and that it was okay to be open. Shirley said she was not sure she could, because she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotions did not make her weak and was healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Afterward, Sara felt her previous confrontation might have been too harsh. She apologized to Shirley for coming on too strong. Shirley said it had been a bit much but that she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed to be doing better. Sara asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to any hidden events or private thoughts of Shirley beyond what Shirley said or what Sara observed/inferred from her behavior.
